Hi Tom — thanks for the heads up. Short answer: we can support a rolling micropatch cadence with staged canaries and an explicit unwind (emergency "unwind" is our term for fast revert) protocol. Longer answer / proposed plan below.

Attachments: micropatch_plan_v1.pdf (internal runbook), netops_quiesce_checklist.csv

Plan highlights (proposed):
- Canary -> 1/8th nodes, then 1/4 -> 1/2 -> full. Wait-for-health checks (5m+ token-sample generation, KV cache rebuild verification).
- Pinning: For micropatches we recommend pinning the model-serving stack to the same minor release (e.g., 2.4.x) and only bumping microdep packages; full minor/major bumps are done in a separate flagged release. This minimizes surface area for rollbacks.
- Maintenance window suggestion: Sat 2026-05-23 02:00–06:00 UTC (lower traffic for your region).
- Rollback/unwind triggers (initial):
  * >2xx server error rate sustained over 10m across canaries
  * >250ms median gen latency regression on 5m sample
  * Token-loss observed in >0.5% of sampled requests (consistency checks fail)
  * NetOps reports network flaps correlated with patching windows
- Automatic fallback: canary failures will block promotion; we will invoke unwind and pin revert on the cluster images.

Action items for HedgeLabs ops:
1) Confirm window (Sat 23rd or Tue 26th) and canary node list.
2) Provide pre-patch traffic baseline snapshots (we'll ingest into our telemetry).

Thanks — quick technical notes from infra/networking perspective:

1) Net quiesce checklist additions (we'll attach to netops_quiesce_checklist.csv):
   - Drain external BGP neighbors for canary nodes; isolate transit to limit churn during AS path changes.
   - Ensure control-plane plane replication lag < 30s before promoting canary.
   - Temporary rate-limits on new session establishment during the 10m post-patch validation window.

2) Image pin strategy:
   - Use image pins at two levels: runtime base image (OS + runtime) and model-serving artifact tag. For micropatches, we patch the runtime base and keep the model-serving artifact tag stable. We create an alternate image tag (e.g., 2.4.3-micro1) and stage it through canaries.

3) Fast unwind path:
   - If canary fails, we trigger an automated rollback job which re-tags nodes to the previous image and restarts the runtime (no config migration). We also hold routing changes until the unwind completes.

4) Edge-case: persistent KV corruption detected during any validation step requires a manual unblock and will move the event into emergency maintenance with an immediate paging cadence.

I'll update the checklist and add the BGP neighbor drain commands. Marcus — please confirm we have capacity for a 1/8th canary slice on Sat morning; otherwise Tue evening might be safer.

Adding the rollback decision matrix and approval gating. Draft summary below (attached: rollback_criteria.md).

Decision matrix (simplified):
- Severity A (auto unwind):
  * Conditions: sustained HTTP 5xx rate >1% across canary for 10m OR median latency >2x baseline for 10m.
  * Action: automatic unwind, suppress promotion, auto-create incident with severity A tag.
- Severity B (operator review, 30m):
  * Conditions: token mismatch or partial degradation affecting <10% of traffic; nonfatal errors in logs.
  * Action: ops review, pause rollout; possible targeted revert for affected host slice.
- Severity C (watch):
  * Conditions: transient spikes <10m, metric noise, nonblocking errors.
  * Action: increase sampling, extended hold; no unwind unless escalated.

Approval flow:
- Auto unwind executes per Severity A triggers.
- For Severity B we require 1x Redwood on-call + 1x HedgeLabs platform owner to approve rollbacks.
- Post-unwind RCA: auto-generated telemetry bundle + priority 72h RCA owner assignment.

Tom — please confirm your on-call person can approve severity B within 30m windows (we'll need a named contact). Also confirm whether your procurement requires DocuSign for any out-of-band SLA exceptions (we added a placeholder DocuSign link in related_links).

-Neha
